_note: Phase 34.4 — the three client-facing cases as driver-override sets. Locked with the client via prosperus-mockup-v5.html. Central's six values ARE the engine's shipped base constants, so a Central run must reproduce the batch-1 numbers exactly; that is asserted, not assumed. Driver semantics, engine bindings and reachability live in scenario-overlay.mjs (DRIVERS) — this file carries values only, so there is one source for each (discipline rule #4).
_trading_realisation_basis: Phase 36.B batch-3 Part 0 — trading_realisation is the one driver in this table that is MEASURED rather than assumed. Central 0.7234 is the volume-weighted realisation of the B1 greedy policy against perfect-foresight sort-and-dispatch capture over realised LT day-ahead prices 2025-07-01 → 2026-06-30 (349 traded days). Downside 0.6535 and Upside 0.8155 are that measurement's own monthly volume-weighted minimum (2025-09) and maximum (2026-05) — an observed band, not a spread invented around the point estimate. The engine constant TRADING_REALISATION.base moved with it, so Central still equals the shipped constant and still patches nothing. Day-ahead component only; remeasure annually.
_direction: fleet_realisation_pct is the fraction of the Baltic pipeline that actually gets built: HIGHER means more competing supply, so Downside carries the highest value. Every other driver reads in the intuitive direction.

downside.label: Downside
downside.note: Pipeline builds out faster than the central dropout assumption, spreads compress, execution and availability slip, and the TSO clears capacity below today's level.

central.label: Central
central.note: The engine's calibrated base case. Every driver equals the shipped engine constant, so no overlay substitution is applied and the output is the unpatched engine's.

upside.label: Upside
upside.note: Pipeline dropout is heavier than central, renewable-driven spread widening runs ahead of BESS smoothing, and post-synchronisation reserve scarcity lifts capacity clearing prices.

litgrid_ltrsc.label: Litgrid L TrSc basis
litgrid_ltrsc.note: Phase 36.D. Not a spread around Central — a named alternative built on the Lithuanian TSO's own published build-out. Every driver is Central's value except the supply basis, which replaces the LT share of projected supply with Litgrid's L TrSc series (1 260 / 2 115 / 2 428 / 2 652 MW at 2028 / 2030 / 2033 / 2035) AS PUBLISHED — no realisation rate, no S-curve, no haircut of ours. The point of the scenario in a client conversation is that it is the TSO's number; layering KKME's build-out assumptions on top would make it neither ours nor theirs. Litgrid forecasts Lithuania only, so EE and LV stay on KKME's projection and Kruonis stays additive (the series is battery storage). Direction vs Central is NOT monotonic: below our Central LT projection at 2028, well above it in conservatism from 2030, where our Central builds 2.0-2.6x more LT capacity than the TSO's own scenario assumes.

sensitivity_only._note: Two further drivers perturbed one-at-a-time in run-sensitivity.mjs. They are not part of the client's scenario table; the down/up values are the 34.4 scope figures.

_named_alternatives_note: Phase 36.D — `order` remains the three client-facing cases locked via prosperus-mockup-v5.html; they are a contract and this phase does not touch them. `litgrid_ltrsc` is a NAMED ALTERNATIVE, not a fourth spread point: it is Central with one driver flipped, and it is excluded from `order` and from the monotonicity invariant because its direction against Central is not monotonic by construction.
